Done. The verified solution is written to **`~/SOLUTION.md`** (self-contained, includes the full source in an appendix), with the working implementation in **`~/quicpath`**.

## Root-cause analysis (what a naive machine gets wrong)

| # | Failure mode | Naive bug | Invariant established |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1 | Reordered bytes bypass 3× budget | credit applied after auth / only to accepted packets | credit `len(datagram)` to the path **before** auth/replay; counters monotonic & saturating |
| 2.2 | NAT rebinding leaks trust/budget | connection-wide `validated`/`received` | `AmpState` is **per 4-tuple**, new path starts `0/0/unvalidated` |
| 2.3 | Migration acted on before auth | switch primary on any packet from a new address | detect from tuple, **commit only after `Open` + replay pass** |
| 2.4 | Retired-ID reuse | single map overwritten | dual-index `CIDTable`; terminal retired state; `retire_prior_to` monotonic |
| 2.5 | Partial key-phase update | flip phase on differing bit, before auth | pure `Classify` → Current/Previous/Next by `pn`; flip only in `Commit` after auth |
| 2.6 | Replays accepted | no window / window updated on receipt | 64-packet window, `Check` then `Commit` after auth |
| 2.7 | Congestion deadlock | connection-wide cwnd, loss never drains | per-path controller, `Reset()` on migration, `OnLoss` clamps at 0 |
| 2.8 | Spoofed-address memory DoS | unbounded path map | `maxPaths` cap |
| 2.9 | Concurrent probes | one challenge slot | per-path `map[[8]byte]time.Time`, response echoed on arrival path |

The security-critical piece is the **ingest order**: resolve CID → create path → **credit bytes** → classify key phase (pure) → authenticate → replay-check → commit replay+keyphase atomically → **only then** migrate/handle frames.

## Verification

```
cd ~/quicpath
go build ./... && go vet ./... && gofmt -l .   # clean
go test -race -count=2 ./...                   # ok  quicpath  1.017s
go test -cover ./...                           # ok  quicpath  coverage: 74.4%
```

31/31 tests pass under the race detector, covering: exact 3× budget, reordered/late credit, retired-ID reuse (CID value and sequence), `retire_prior_to` monotonicity, `active_connection_id_limit`, NAT-rebinding independent budget, unauthenticated non-migration, concurrent path probes, partial key-phase update, replay rejection, congestion reset-on-migration, loss unblocking, and path-cap enforcement.
